transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Cascade - Head of ML), Derek Huang (Cascade - Platform), Marisol Vega (Cascade - Procurement)
Title: Renewal & expansion check-in - Cascade Systems

Summary: quick checkin on renewal, adding regions, and committed capacity. Discussed pricing, KMS, SOC2, and next steps.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): All right, everyone thanks for hopping on. Agenda is quick — renewals, capacity, and the multi-region ask. How's that sound?
[00:18] Priya (Cascade): Sounds good. We're under timeline for our EU launch in Q3, want to make sure latency is good and cost doesn't explode.
[00:36] Lena: Got it. Samir will cover perf, I'll cover commercial and contract. Samir, quick update on the Dedicated pool perf from the pilot?
[00:52] Samir (Redwood SE): Yes, so from the pilot we saw p95 gen latency around 220ms on US region with our xG-16 configs, when batch sizes are tuned. EU was a bit higher — roughly 320ms — because you had a higher seq length and we had cold cache during the runs. There's also a KV cash issue in the proto run — the transcriber might say K-V cash, but it's KV cache.
[01:20] Derek (Cascade): We noticed that, yeah. Our prompts have a lot of context, avg 1.2k tokens. Is there guidance for quantization or model variants to reduce cost?
[01:34] Samir: For that profile we typically recommend a mixed strategy: keep a higher-fidelity model for low-volume high-importance calls, and a quantized variant for bulk. Also prefix caching helps — Redwood's prefix/kv approach should reduce repeated tokens. We can suggest a quantized config that preserves quality for your prompt set.
[01:50] Priya: Quality is critical — we can't have hallucinations increase. Any regression risk with quantization?
[02:02] Samir: Small risk, but we do per-prompt evals. We'll run your top 20 prompts through the quantized candidate and compare. If regression > threshold we don't recommend switch.
[02:18] Marisol (Procurement): On the business side, we're looking at committed 12-month pricing. Need visibility on total cost. Also need SOC2 and KMS commitments — we require customer-managed keys if possible.
[02:36] Lena: Understood. We support KMS integrations and can document the flow. We'll include SOC 2 type II artifacts and our encryption in transit and at rest docs. Samir, can you note the KMS integration caveats?
[02:50] Samir: Yes, we have a couple patterns: Redwood Private (V-P-C) option where the control plane is customer-managed, and dedicated capacity with KMS integration for key wrapping. There is a slight increase in latency when using customer KMS for token decryption at call time, but it's usually in the single-digit ms.
[03:12] Derek: Single-digit ms is okay. More important is audit logs and retention. We need per-request audit trails forwarded into our SIEM for compliance. Do you have examples?
[03:28] Lena: Yes, we can forward audit logs and have per-route tracing. We'll share our log format and a sample sink config for Splunk/Datadog.
[03:40] Priya: On regions — we need EU (Frankfurt) and APAC (Singapore) in addition to US. Is cross-region replication supported for cache warmup?
[03:56] Samir: Cross-region cache replication isn't automatic out of the box — we can do warmup strategies, pre-warming with synthetic traffic, and cross-region fallbacks. There's a design tradeoff: replicate KV cache increases cost and complexity. For EU launch we'd recommend provisioned dedicated shards in each region.
[04:16] Priya: Provisioned shards meaning dedicated GPUs per region?
[04:22] Samir: Correct. Dedicated pools per region, pinned model versions, autoscaling policies per region. That gives predictable p95s.
[04:32] Marisol: That will increase spend. We need a clear delta between our current hosted usage and committed Dedicated.
[04:40] Lena: We'll provide a delta estimate. Samir will run a perf + cost model for 3-region Dedicated vs hybrid (hosted for APAC, dedicated for EU+US).
[04:53] Derek: Timeline-wise, procurement needs a PO by mid-July to align with engineering rollout. Is that doable?
[04:59] Marisol: mid-July is our target.
[05:06] Lena: We can push contract + quote by next week — aim for 2027-06-07 for the pricing doc.
[05:14] Priya: Also wanted to ask about fallbacks: if a region is constrained, can we route to another region and still meet SLAs? Latency will be higher but better than errors.
[05:28] Samir: Yes, Redwood has smart routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants or different regions. You can set policy per route — latency-first or cost-first. In practice, we fall back to slightly smaller model variant if you allow it.
[05:44] Priya: OK. For our sensitive flows, we can't fall back to non-EU data paths because of data residency.
[05:52] Samir: Then you'd configure strict region pinning for those routes. Fallback would only go to warm standby in-region or failover to a private dedicated pool.
[06:04] Derek: Any outage history or SLA for Dedicated? We need 99.9+ uptime in contract.
[06:12] Lena: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed targets; we'll include our SLA doc. Historically we've had sub-0.1% downtime for dedicated customers this year, but I'll send the reliability numbers.
[06:24] Marisol: For legal, we'll need indemnities and standard vendor terms — we'll push redlines after review.
[06:32] Lena: Noted. We'll have legal loop in once we share draft.
[06:40] Speaker 1: (inaudible) benchmarks link?
[06:44] Lena: Yes — short pause — we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet link in the follow-up (the pilot runs and raw logs).
[06:52] Priya: Can you also include a summary of expected token unit costs once we move to dedicated? We want to compare to our current hosted per-token rates.
[07:02] Lena: Absolutely. We'll include per-token and per-hour GPU amortized numbers in the quote.
[07:10] Derek: For the pilot — what's needed from our side?
[07:14] Samir: Ideally: top 20 prompts, traffic distribution, and sample payloads. We'll run both quantized and full models and return a perf/quality report. Priya, you said you'd provide top 20 prompts?
[07:26] Priya: Yes I'll get that by Friday (2027-06-05).
[07:30] Samir: Great. We'll then schedule a <30 minute runbook call to walk through how to send traffic and run evaluations. Suggest 2027-06-09 for that session.
[07:40] Marisol: Procurement will want final pricing and a statement of work for sign-off.
[07:46] Lena: We'll include SOW language in the draft and outline commit levels.
[07:52] Priya: One more question — any known regressions when moving to a quantized 4-bit variant for our use-case?
[07:58] Samir: In our internal tests, some instruction-heavy prompts occasionally lose formatting or exhibit slight style drift. We'll run regression checks and include examples. If that happens, we can keep a hybrid: most traffic on quantized, critical flows on full model.
[08:14] Derek: For data exfil concerns, we need confirmation of no PII logging.
[08:20] Lena: We can confirm that customer data is not used for training and retention policies can be configured per customer. We'll share the retention SLA.
[08:30] Priya: All right, sounds like we have a path. Quick recap?
[08:35] Lena: Recap — Redwood to send updated pricing and SOC2/KMS docs by 2027-06-04, Samir to provide perf/cost estimate by 2027-06-07, Priya to send prompts by 2027-06-05, schedule runbook on 2027-06-09, Marisol to confirm PO window by 2027-06-08, and Redwood legal will draft contract extension for 12-month committed capacity by 2027-06-10.
[09:00] Marisol: Sounds good.
[09:03] Derek: One small note — we might evaluate a hybrid where APAC stays hosted for now to save costs, and we add APAC Dedicated later — is that flexible?
[09:14] Lena: Absolutely flexible. We'll provide hybrid vs full dedicated cost comparisons.
[09:20] Priya: Thank you everyone. Any blockers from Redwood?
[09:25] Samir: No blockers — we just need the prompt set and permission to run the evals.
[09:31] Lena: Great, we'll follow up in an email with attachments and links.
[09:36] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:38] Lena: Thanks all — bye.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (V-P-C, K-V cash), speaker overlaps, and auto-caption punctuation is imperfect. References shared in chat during call: "pilot-benchmarks.xlsx" (link), "SOC2_summary.pdf" (link), contract template (link).

End of transcript.
